A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including proofs, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic-chair experiments, node-classification results on eight datasets, and ModelNet10/40 graph-classification analyses.

after.justification: v6 retains original synthetic, node-classification and ModelNet40 results, and adds Laplacian-spectrum analyses of the eight node datasets.

M1.justification: The GNN/MNN architectures, graph-construction kernels and spectral regularizer remain unchanged. Relabeling the low-pass filter definition as Assumption 1 preserves its mathematical conditions; the theoretical revisions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions document the synthetic chair, eight node-classification datasets, and ModelNet10/40 graph tasks. The new spectrum analysis reuses existing graphs. ModelNet10 remains in the experimental appendix despite removal of its generalization plot.

E2.justification: No external comparison method is added or removed. The retained experiments compare the same GNN configurations; newly cited manifold-network methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces a diagnostic procedure examining the 100 largest Laplacian eigenvalues for each node dataset. The retained classification experiments keep their splits, training budgets, accuracy metric and cross-entropy loss.

E4.justification: v6 adds a spectral diagnostic intended to support the manifold assumption. It removes v4 Figure 8's ModelNet10 analysis across graph sizes and regularization settings, while retaining the node-level sensitivity studies and ModelNet40 architecture analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 independent runs for node experiments and five random partitions with averages and standard deviations for ModelNet experiments. No change in repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation practices is documented.

E6.justification: v6 adds eight eigenvalue-spectrum curves in Figure 5 and removes the ModelNet10 output-gap results in v4 Figure 8. All 92 numerical rows in the appendix linear-fit tables match, including the Arxiv two-layer, 64-feature correlation of -0.9980. The removed summary correlation table repeats retained appendix values.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and their supporting proofs receive substantive revisions: epsilon factors become square-root-epsilon factors with corresponding bandwidth-exponent adjustments, and d=2 receives a separate rate. v6 also adds Lipschitz density regularity, strengthens Proposition 3's stated assumptions, revises eigenfunction-bound algebra, and adds Corollary 1 with a proof comparing empirical risks on two sampled graphs.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain the same claims: manifold-based generalization bounds for node and graph tasks, decreasing gaps with graph size, dependence on spectral continuity, and a discriminability–generalization trade-off.

C2.justification: New Appendix I interprets eigenvalue decay as support for modeling the real-world graphs through low-dimensional manifolds. v6 also explains reduced discriminability through a smaller hypothesis class and states that the analysis can accommodate different feature counts across layers.

D1.justification: v6 omits v4's ModelNet10 passage specifying coordinate inputs, training graphs with 20–100 sampled points, and comparison against a 100-node testing graph. The shared appendix retains optimizer settings, filter counts, hardware, training time and dataset-access instructions. This reduces documented detail without establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: v6 adds Chew et al. (2023, 2024) and Johnson et al. (2025) to the manifold-network discussion, plus Talmon, Peyre and Osher references supporting manifold modeling. The established positioning against graphon and other generalization analyses remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v6 condenses the experimental narrative and conclusion, numbers sections and appendices, moves supplementary reference/filter discussions before experimental details, and adds an Impact Statement. Many blank section references are resolved, although Appendix G contains unresolved figure references.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column layout. v4 Figures 4–6 are combined into v6 Figure 3, the filter illustration is redrawn, and the regularization plots receive logarithmic vertical scales. Other changes include removal of the graph-construction illustration and ModelNet10 plot, addition of the spectrum figure, and extensive figure/table relocation.

improvement.justification: The more explicit theorem conditions, separate dimensional cases and new two-graph corollary improve the precision and usefulness of the theoretical presentation. Section and appendix references also improve navigation. These gains are partly offset by removal of the ModelNet10 generalization plot and its testing details, supporting a limited overall improvement.
